From 46c6d45d7875a0328258a574e376ae75f7b2a64b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2015 23:35:25 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] cxlflash: off by one bug in cxlflash_show_port_status()

The > should be >= or we read one element past the end of the array.

Fixes: c21e0bbfc485 ('cxlflash: Base support for IBM CXL Flash Adapter')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Matthew R. Ochs <mrochs@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: James Bottomley <JBottomley@Odin.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
index 458ed838f83a..fde2ba9342dc 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
@@ -586,7 +586,7 @@ static ssize_t cxlflash_show_port_status(struct device *dev,
 	u64 *fc_regs;
 
 	rc = kstrtouint((attr->attr.name + 4), 10, &port);
-	if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
+	if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
 		return 0;
 
 	fc_regs = &afu->afu_map->global.fc_regs[port][0];
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c`**
- The condition in the `cxlflash_show_port_status` function was modified from `if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))` to `if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))`. This change ensures that the function does not attempt to access an element beyond the end of the `fc_regs` array, thus fixing an off-by-one bug.

### Relationships
The modification in the `main.c` file directly addresses a bug related to array bounds checking. By changing the comparison operator from `>` to `>=`, the patch prevents the function from reading one element past the end of the array, which could lead to undefined behavior or crashes. This fix is linked to a previous commit identified by the hash `c21e0bbfc485`, which introduced the base support for the IBM CXL Flash Adapter, indicating that the bug was introduced in that commit.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
```
Reason:
The use of the `>` operator allows the `port` variable to exceed the valid range of indices for the `fc_regs` array, which can lead to accessing an out-of-bounds element and potentially causing undefined behavior or a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
```
Reason:
Changing the comparison operator from `>` to `>=` ensures that the function correctly checks for valid indices, preventing access to memory beyond the allocated array and thus avoiding the out-of-bounds access issue.
